lines: Thunder shook the fletching table until every bowstring hummed.
We stayed inside and counted the seconds after each flash.
The bell sounded small under that sky.
Lightning struck close enough to fill the workshop with blue light.
I unstrung the good bows before the damp reached them.
Nobody wanted to stand near a window.
The children covered their ears while we checked every room.
One strike split the old tree beside the target lane.
Rain found three leaks we did not know we had.
I kept dry feathers wrapped while others watched the doors.
When the storm moved east, the whole village breathed again.
The golem stood in the square through all of it.
We found a frightened cat beneath the arrow rack.
Every crack of thunder made someone ask whether the bell had rung.
The roof held, though one shutter did not.
I checked on the neighbors before I checked the workshop.
The air smelled burned long after the last flash.
We will ground the new target posts better than the old ones.
Tonight I want a quiet sky and a dry string.
Everyone near me came through it. That matters more than the soaked supplies.
I checked feathers, string, and dry sticks for sparks, then checked faces for smoke and <dark_gray><wavy>fear</wavy></dark_gray>.
We passed water hand to hand until our arms stopped feeling like ours.
Fresh arrows can wait. People come first.
Smoke reached the fletching table before the flames did.
I dragged the feather sacks outside because they catch too easily.
Someone broke the workshop window to clear the smoke.
The bell brought every bucket in the village.
We found the missing child beside the well.
One wall is blackened, but it is still standing.
I will never store glue that close to the stove again.
The golem carried water in hands bigger than our buckets.
Ash settled on every arrow I had finished that morning.
We kept the lane clear for people leaving the smoke.
The animals panicked before most of us saw the flames.
A wet blanket saved the bow rack.
Nobody slept until every ember was cold.
We lost supplies, not neighbors.
The workshop smells burned, even with the doors open.
Next time the buckets stay filled.
I can remake arrows. I am grateful that is all I need to remake.
During a raid, fresh arrows can wait. Who makes it behind a door matters more.
The horns stopped, but my hands still expect another wave.
We counted living neighbors before we counted arrows.
Raiders found barred doors and a bell that would not stop.
I saw fear cross the square, then courage get there first.
Half the quivers came back empty.
The north fence gave way sooner than anyone expected.
Someone kept the children below the workshop until it was quiet.
I passed arrows through a broken shutter until the bundle was gone.
The golem held the road while we pulled the wounded inside.
Crossbow bolts are still buried in the target posts.
We should move spare strings closer to the center.
One clear warning from the fields bought us precious time.
The roofs gave our archers a view and nowhere to hide.
I could tell each wave by how quickly the bow rack emptied.
The last horn sounded farther away than the first.
We recovered more arrows than I expected and fewer than I hoped.
Nobody should guard a gate alone next time.
The village is standing because people chose one another.
I am tired of making arrows for raids, but I will make more.
Night trouble found the loose latch by the fletching table first.
I listened beyond bow range for anyone calling from the dark.
Dawn gave us enough light to count wounds and missing blocks.
Every shadow looked alive until the sun rose.
We lit the target lane so nobody crossed it unseen.
Zombies reached the pens before the bell woke half the village.
I fired by sound once and hated the feeling.
The moon gave us just enough light to see movement.
Someone carried lanterns along the wall while we watched the fields.
I kept one arrow nocked and both ears open.
The children slept through more of it than the adults did.
A spider came over the roof where no one was watching.
We learned which corners the torchlight misses.
The golem found trouble before our eyes did.
Nobody wanted to open a door for a knock they could not place.
The eastern path needs lamps before another night like that.
I found three spent arrows after sunrise.
My hands only shook when the sky began to brighten.
We are fixing every latch before sunset.
Tonight the bows stay strung beside the door.
The wind threw sand through every crack. I am still cleaning grit out of the bowstring.
We tied cloth over our faces before crossing the square.
The fletching table looked buried by midday.
A hard wind teaches you which doors only pretend to close.
Nobody could see the next house for a while.
Sand stripped feathers from arrows left outside.
We followed the wall to reach the neighbors.
The bell vanished into the noise of the wind.
I wrapped every finished bow before the grit reached it.
One roof lost enough blocks to fill the lane.
The animals crowded together before the storm arrived.
We found an old man by following his cough.
Every hinge in the village needs cleaning.
The target faces east now, whether I meant it to or not.
Dry wind can still ruin dry gear.
I kept counting voices when I could not count faces.
The children are safe and very tired of sand.
We marked doors with rope so people could find them.
I will be finding grit in the feathers for weeks.
The sky is clear again, but nobody trusts the wind yet.
Fresh arrows can wait. Warm hands, clear paths, and full hearths come first.
Snow piled against the workshop door before noon.
We tied a rope between houses when the paths disappeared.
Cold makes bowstrings brittle and people quiet.
I watched for footprints that stopped too soon.
The hearth stayed lit all night.
We brought the animals closer before the drifts grew deep.
Someone cleared the well three times.
The fletching table became a place for hot bowls and blankets.
Powder snow swallowed the target lane completely.
We found two travelers by the lantern they carried.
Every spare feather stayed wrapped and dry.
The roofs groaned whenever the wind changed.
Children took turns keeping the smallest fire fed.
Nobody went outside alone after dark.
I snapped the ice from the arrowheads at sunrise.
The village paths are narrow tunnels now.
We checked every home before we slept.
The storm took a roof, but no lives.
Keep the fires fed until the last path is open.
